name: sstp-client
desc: SSTP (Microsoft's Remote Access Solution for PPP over SSL) client
why: Opens the door to SSTP, Microsoft's PPP-over-TLS VPN protocol, which is rarely examined outside Windows.

brief.what_it_is: sstp-client is a client implementation of the Secure Socket Tunneling Protocol (SSTP), which lets a Linux or macOS machine make a remote-access VPN connection to a Microsoft Windows server. The installed executable is sstpc. The project's own page describes it as allowing remote access via SSTP VPN to Microsoft Windows 2008 Server. The README itself is only a pointer to the wiki, so the input and output details beyond that are not documented in what I could read. The brew description calls SSTP Microsoft's Remote Access Solution for PPP over SSL.
brief.why_it_exists: The project page gives no explicit motivation. It exists to provide a non-Windows client for SSTP, the VPN protocol Microsoft's Windows remote access uses.
brief.how_it_works: Not explained in the pages I could read. The brew description says SSTP is PPP carried over SSL, and the repository is tagged pppd, and the brew caveat says sstpc reads PPP options from /etc/ppp/options, which suggests it hands the PPP session to the system's pppd. The README does not state this mechanism itself.
brief.install_notes: Beyond brew install: the brew caveat says sstpc reads PPP configuration options from /etc/ppp/options, and if that file does not exist it should be created with sudo touch /etc/ppp/options. This came from the brew metadata, not from the project README, so it is not a command I saw on the project pages. No other hardware, account, or runtime requirements were visible.
brief.standout: Most VPN clients people run are WireGuard or OpenVPN, but this one speaks Microsoft's SSTP, which is usually only seen inside Windows, so it is a rare look at that protocol from the outside. The scout note frames SSTP as PPP over TLS; the project page says SSL, and the wiki that might have detail was empty.
brief.status: Unknown to a degree. The GitLab page shows the project was created May 16, 2021, and the license is GPL v2.0 or later. I saw no last release date, last commit date, or changelog entry on the fetched pages, so I cannot confirm whether it is actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The README is a single line pointing to the wiki, and the wiki home page loaded empty, so there is little documentation available. The project page says it targets Linux and Mac OS-X and Windows 2008 Server, and I saw nothing about Windows 2016 or later servers. Brew's caveat implies manual PPP configuration setup. I could not verify the build or any usage steps.
quotes: A client implementation of Secure Socket Tunneling Protocol (SSTP) for Linux / Mac OS-X that allows remote access via SSTP VPN to Microsoft Windows 2008 Server.
To learn more about this project, read the wiki.
